TRANSCRIBED BY EYE FROM THE PAGE IMAGES, 2026-09-06 (p_288).
The Internet Archive item has NO OCR text layer because the document is
cursive manuscript, not print; automatic OCR was never going to produce
anything. The jp2 images were downloaded, converted to greyscale, and read
directly. Leaves 3, 4, 6 and 8 of the scan are inverted 180 degrees and were
rotated before reading.

THIS TRANSCRIPT IS A READING, NOT A FACSIMILE. Deletions the writer struck
through are omitted; interlined insertions are silently incorporated;
[square brackets] mark an uncertain reading. Underlining in the original is
marked ___like this___ where it carries meaning (the writer states that
suggestions repeated in several letters are the underlined ones).

NOTE ON WHICH CAMP THIS IS. The report names Lac St. Joseph, Rock Island,
Corbett Island and the Rapids: it is the YMCA of Montreal's ORIGINAL camp at
Lake Saint-Joseph, Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard (the camp later called Otoreke),
NOT Kanawana, which did not exist until 1910. Every place name below belongs
to that site.
============================================================

[1]
Seventh Annual Report of the Current Camp Committee.

                                   Montreal, Dec. 10th '00.

To the Chairman Permanent Camp Committee.

Dear Sir:--

     We, the members of the Current Camp Committee, take very great pleasure
in presenting this report in that we think we have come through the banner
year in the Camp's history.

     Altogether our Committee has handled three parties during the season;
the 24th of May party, the regular Summer party and a special Fall party
towards the end of September. The 24th party composed of some of the most
prominent members of the Association to the number of twenty four, including
the President, Treasurer and four Directors, was, we think, a most enjoyable
affair, lasting four days. The Camp should profit very materially as a result
of this outing as the impression formed by the "Fathers of the Association"
was a very favorable one.

     The summer season was a record one in

[2]
many ways. The attendance of __ members shows an increase of __ over last
season. Among those visiting camp were many new men who were without
exception, as far as it is in our power to ascertain, well pleased with their
stay, and hope to go out again.

     Evening concerts were very frequent during the season, the campers
falling into the spirit of things quite enthusiastically; fishing and
exploring parties were without number, and the Annual Regatta was a feature
which will long be remembered by those who were priviledged to be present.

     Those who were at Camp at the time of the Ste Agathe Regatta attended
that affair in a body, arranging for their own transportation and taking the
chef along with them. In all, our Campers captured eleven prizes and did much
towards advertising the camp at that place. Doubtless had the Campers had
skiffs at their disposal and so been able to compete in the rowing events the
number of prizes taken into camp would have been much larger.

     The fall party numbering twelve left town on Sept. 21st and returned
Sept. 26 -- being unanimous in declaring they had had an a1 good time.

[3]
A series of photos taken on this outing of some of the members in duck suits
will make an interesting illustration for next year's prospectus. The chef
was a different [type] from the man who was out with the other two parties;
and according to our informants is an artist in his trade and well worth
considering for future occasions.

     We beg to hand you herewith a copy of the prospectus as issued by this
Committee for the past season.

     On Oct. 20th this Committee sent a letter to every member of the
Association who had been to Camp during 1900, calling for criticisms
favorable or otherwise and also suggestions. The replies received were almost
without exception favorable and many were exceedingly complimentary. Some
notably those who had attended camp towards the close of the summer season
complained about the manner in which the meals were cooked and served up, but
in every case stated that it was not a fault of this committee, as the food
supplied was of the best, the trouble emanating entirely from the chef.

     This committee feel that this is a serious matter and ask that a more
proficient chef be secured in future.

[4]
     It will be well to give some of the suggestions from the letters received
in answer to our circular letter of Oct. 20th. Many of these suggestions are
repeatedly mentioned in the letters, and where such is the case, will be found
underlined.

  ___Get a new chimney cap___, present one is too small and fills the house
  with smoke (one friend says "breaking the rule of no smoking allowed in
  Camp").

  ___The same man should be in charge of Camp all summer___

  Camp should be in order before opening for the season.

  ___Permanent wharf___, and a good one. Where is the one advertised in the
  accompanying prospectus?

  Camp should supply some indoor games for evenings and wet days

  ___Change position of tents___.

  ___Prepare other ground for tents similar to "High Bluff"___ using blocks in
  ground for poles to rest on so that they can't sink & thereby put the tents
  out of shape.

[5]
  ___Provide flies for the tents___ as they are all leaking more or less.

  ___Remove Ice-House___, up nearer to Kitchen, it now spoils view from
  gallery, & there, would be more handy, causing less waste.

  ___Get an older Cook___, a man who has passed thirty-five and one who knows
  his place. One man claims that when he remonstrated with this season's chef
  about the dishes coming to the table unwashed, it almost came to blows.

  Spring water should be brought by pump to the house

  Put up shelves in the Ice-house.

  Ice-house is not built properly, should have a saw-dust lining at least six
  inches deep all around. Ice raised from floor a foot; this would make a
  genuine refrigerator.

  It should be forbidden to deposit fish entrails & other refuse in the lake
  at the kitchen wharf.

  We are informed that Bergin the carter sells liquor.

[6]
  Ground around house should be terraced

  Camp should provide a couple of canoes and also a full sized war canoe

  Boats should be in perfect repair befor camp opens. Four leaked all the past
  season

  Firewood should be neatly piled near kitchen

  ___There should be a dark room at camp___.

  Clean up Island

  Make an athletic field on Corbett Island

  Why not name the camp island & also the one opposite, that is now "called"
  "Corbett Is"?

  White oilcloth should be provided for table

  Camp should buy decent diving boards in town and bring them out.

  ___Arrange to have milk delivered on time in the mornings___, and not have
  breakfast waiting until half past nine; Bergeron fault.

  ___There should be covered waggon and carriage for transportation of
  campers & baggage___, several men have been caught at different times in
  rain storms.

[7]
  Camp should supply more blankets, two to each man.

  There should be a large hole dug at a short distance from the house to
  deposit the refuse in; they should not be dumped at the kitchen door.

  It should be forbidden to dig for worms so close to the house as has been
  the custom.

  It would be better to have smaller tables for dining, then all could be
  served better & a table reserved for late arrivals who have been off fishing.

  The camp should have a shelter or lean to of some kind down on Rock Island
  to "rough it" in while fishing.

  ___Purchase Lumbermen's Shanty at the Rapids.___

  Purchase all the Islands in Lac St. Joseph.

  Shelves are needed in the worst way in the kitchen.

  There should be a proper pantry & Ice-house built near kitchen.

  Camp Should purchase Rock Island

[8]
  ___Cutlery at camp is abominable___. Silver what there ever was of it is all
  worn off & "brass spoons" is now more applicable to them. Camp should
  provide Aluminum spoons and forks, all sizes are needed & can easily be got
  & cheaply.

  Soup plates are not the only kind of enamelled plates made. Why not have
  dinner plates at camp?

  ___Diving Rock is an ideal swimming place and should be equipped with a
  spring board___.

     This committee trusts that these suggestions will have the careful
consideration of your Committee. They also hope and pray that the camp may
continue to grow as it has done in the past, and wish to thank you and your
fellow committee men for the trust & honour conferred on us in placing its
guidance in our hands for the past season.

              The whole of which is respectfully Submitted
                   signed on behalf of the committee

Frank [L.] Benedict                    [monogram] Dawson
    Chairman                              Secy.

--- ON THE TWO SIGNATURES ---
The surname DAWSON is unambiguous. The initials before it are a single
interlocking monogram inside a large enclosing loop and CANNOT be resolved
from this scan; the second letter reads as a capital B, the first as R or A.
This transcript therefore does not assert whose Dawson it is.
Frank Benedict's middle initial is a flourished capital read here as L, on
the strength of the 1898 Camp Jubilee photograph caption which names FRANK L.
BENEDICT and RALPH H. DAWSON together (f_0021, f_0930); B cannot be ruled out
from the signature alone.
